title: Financial Management in Construction Companies: The Role of Guarantees as a Mechanism to Address Payment Delays
content: Background: Delayed interim payments destabilize contractors’ working capital and transmit liquidity shocks to subcontractors and suppliers. Yet construction guarantees differ markedly in their beneficiaries, triggers and capacity to make funds available. Objective: To critically examine the financial role of guarantees in payment-delay management and develop a conceptual framework that aligns contractual security with cash-flow continuity. Methods: A targeted international documentary synthesis of traceable peer-reviewed studies published primarily during 2020–2026 was complemented by authoritative payment-security instruments and legal rules. This is a methodological design article, not a completed PRISMA systematic review or empirical validation. Results: The synthesis distinguishes performance security, advance-payment security, payment bonds, owner-backed payment security, ring-fenced project accounts and digitally enabled payment administration. It proposes the Payment Security–Liquidity Alignment Framework (PSLAF), organized around four dimensions and twelve candidate indicators, a guarantee–beneficiary matrix, scenario-based liquidity equations and an explicit validation protocol. Discussion: Guarantees protect different parties and cannot independently cure inadequate certification, unfunded payment obligations or power asymmetry. Conclusions: Contract security should be evaluated by beneficiary fit, actual access to funds and timeliness, rather than by its nominal amount alone; empirical testing across jurisdictions is required before effectiveness or optimal coverage can be claimed.
